info.title: Personalitify API
info.description:
Central backend of the Personalitify ecosystem. Every client — web, the future Rust
desktop application, mobile and third-party integrations — uses this same API.

**Conventions**

- Successful responses are wrapped as `{ "data": …, "meta": … }`.
- Failures are `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }`. Branch on
  `code`; `message` is localized from `Accept-Language` (`tr` default, `en`).
- Identifiers are UUID strings. Instants are ISO 8601 in UTC. Calendar dates are
  `YYYY-MM-DD` in the user's time zone. Times of day are `HH:mm`.
- Synchronized resources carry an integer `version`. Send it back as `baseVersion`
  when updating; a stale version is merged field by field or rejected with
  `409 VERSION_CONFLICT`.
- Breaking changes are published under a new path prefix; this document describes
  `/api/v1`.

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: Statistics of a calendar period next to the period before it. Every figure is counted from the user’s own records at request time, in their time zone; nothing is estimated, and there is no composite score.

tags.name: Achievements
tags.description: Experience points, levels and achievements. XP is granted by the server from the user’s own records by fixed rules — once per record, and taken back when the record is undone. Achievements are unlocked when their figure is reached and are never taken back. Clients cannot grant either.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Data export, security log and account deletion.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Registration, sign-in, token refresh and session management. Access tokens are short-lived JWTs; refresh tokens are opaque, single-use and rotated on every refresh. Browser clients (`clientType: "web"`) receive the refresh token as an HttpOnly cookie; all other clients receive it in the response body.

tags.name: Calendar
tags.description: Events and the unified calendar. `GET /calendar` merges events, tasks and habits into display-ready items positioned in the user’s time zone. Timed events keep their wall-clock time in their own zone on every occurrence.

tags.name: Categories
tags.description: User-defined labels shared by habits, goals, tasks and calendar events.

tags.name: Goals
tags.description: Short- and long-term goals with milestones, sub-goals, reviews and links to habits and tasks. Responses carry a `computed` object with the derived progress.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Tasks with priorities, dates, planned time blocks, subtasks and recurrence. A repeating task is a series of individual tasks: completing one creates the next occurrence.

tags.name: Dashboard
tags.description: Everything the personal dashboard shows, in one request. All figures are derived from the user’s own records at request time. The widget layout is part of the settings (`settings.dashboard`).

tags.name: Devices
tags.description: Client installations registered to the account. A device is registered automatically when it signs in; its id is returned as `tokens.deviceId`.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: The user’s ordered log of changes. Every create, update and delete of a synchronized entity is one event with the next sequence number. The same events are pushed over the realtime connection; this endpoint is how a client reads what it missed.

tags.name: Focus
tags.description: A timer for focus sessions and breaks. All instants are set by the server: clients ask it to start, pause, resume and finish, and draw the countdown from `endsAt` and `serverTime`. A user has one active session at a time, on whichever device it was started. A session that reaches its planned length is completed by the server.

tags.name: Habits
tags.description: Habits, their schedules and what was recorded for them day by day. Every date is a calendar day in the user’s configured time zone; the server decides what "today" is and reports it in the responses.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Liveness and readiness probes. No authentication.

tags.name: Journal
tags.description: Journal entries and notes written in Markdown, with tags, search and a history of earlier contents. Entries are private to the account; lists return previews instead of bodies, and no preview at all when the user hides sensitive previews.

tags.name: Mood
tags.description: How each day felt: one entry per calendar day in the user’s time zone. Notes are private to the account.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: What the server wants to tell the user: reminders for habits, tasks, goals and events, unlocked achievements and timers that ran out. Notifications are made by the server according to the user’s notification settings; clients list them, mark them as read and delete them. Each carries its kind and values, not a finished sentence.

tags.name: Platform
tags.description: What a client asks the server about itself: whether a newer version exists, whether its own version is still supported, and the settings the server can change without a new release. These endpoints need no sign-in, so a client can ask before the user has an account. The server neither builds nor hosts applications; a release is a record that a version exists and where it can be fetched.

tags.name: Administration
tags.description: Managing releases and remote configuration. Requires the `admin` role, which is granted from the command line (`npm run admin:grant -- <email>`), never through the API. Every change is written to the security log of the administrator who made it.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: Preferences that follow the user to every client: language, theme, time zone, date and time formats, notification and privacy preferences.

tags.name: Sync
tags.description: Keeps a device that stores its own copy of the data in step with the account. A device starts from a snapshot, then repeatedly pulls the changes after its cursor, pushes the operations it queued while offline, and confirms how far it has come. See docs/architecture/synchronization.md.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: The signed-in account and its profile.

get.summary: Statistics of a week, month, quarter or year
get.description: Returns the whole calendar period that contains `date` (default: today, in the user’s time zone), with habit, task and goal figures, a step-by-step series for charts, and the same key figures for the previous period.

range.description: The whole calendar period, first to last day

previousRange.description: The period of the same kind right before it

complete.description: False while the period is still running; counts are then not final

series.description: The period step by step: days of a week or month, weeks of a quarter, months of a year

due.description: Due days of fixed-schedule habits that could be judged: completed or missed. Skipped and postponed days, today while it is open, and future days are left out

rate.description: completed / due; null when nothing was due

unit.description: What due, completed and missed count: days, or periods of a flexible habit

habits.description: Totals cover fixed-schedule habits; `items` lists every habit in its own unit

completed.description: Tasks finished on a day of the period

due.description: Tasks whose due date lies in the period, cancelled ones left out

dueCompleted.description: Of those, the ones that are done

onTime.description: Finished tasks with a due date, finished on or before it

late.description: Finished tasks with a due date, finished after it

overdueOpen.description: Open tasks past their due date right now

expected.description: Share of the time from start to target date that has passed, in percent

pace.description: percent against expected, with ten points of tolerance; null without a target date

tasksCompleted.description: Linked tasks finished during the period

highlights.description: Observations made by fixed, documented rules from the figures in `params`

get.description: Rules (XP): a completed habit day 10 · a finished task 5, high priority 10 · a milestone 15 · a completed goal 50 · 2 per five minutes of a completed focus session, at most 24 per session · writing in the journal 5 once a day · recording the mood 2 once a day.

week.description: XP of the last seven days, today included

levelXp.description: Total XP at which this level started

nextLevelXp.description: Total XP at which the next level starts

needed.description: XP still missing for the next level

progress.description: Share of the way to the next level, 0 to 1

current.description: The metric so far, never more than the target

date.description: The user’s calendar date the XP belongs to

recent.description: The latest XP earned, newest first

get.description: Returns every record the account owns, grouped by type, in the same resource format the API uses elsewhere. Credentials and token hashes are never included.

get.summary: Get the unified calendar for a date range
get.description: At most 62 days. Returns every occurrence of repeating events, tasks by their time block or due date, habits on the days they are due, and the pairs of timed items that overlap.

Send the returned `cursor` next time; while `hasMore` is true, ask again at once. Answers `CURSOR_EXPIRED` (410) when the cursor is older than the history that is kept: start again from a snapshot.

seq.description: Position of the entity’s latest change

data.description: The entity as it is now; null for a deletion

post.summary: Confirm how far the device has applied the changes
post.description: A device’s position never moves back; a lower value is ignored.

oldestCursor.description: Positions below this have left the history; catching up from them is not possible

cursor.description: The last position this device confirmed

behind.description: How many positions the device has not confirmed yet

canCatchUp.description: False: the device must start again from a snapshot

post.description: Each operation is a request the client would have made while online: a method, a path below the API prefix and a body, with an id (`opId`) the client chose. Operations are carried out in order, each exactly like that request, and each gets its own outcome — one failing does not stop the next. Sending an operation again with the same `opId` returns its first outcome (`replayed: true`) without doing anything twice. Sign-in, account, device and synchronization operations cannot be pushed. At most 100 operations per request, and 30 requests a minute.

status.description: The HTTP status the request would have been answered with

replayed.description: True: carried out before; this is the stored outcome

cursor.description: The account’s position after the operations

opId.description: Chosen by the client; unique per operation
